newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end down but off day's low.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end down but off day's low.

text.p: The Singapore stock market rebounded off the day's low after Tokyo stocks posted a strong recovery on short-covering in late trade on Monday, dealers said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended off 9.91 points at 2,232.40. Turnover was heavy at around 204 million shares, with gainers lagging losers by 164 to 215.

Dealers said Malaysian shares stole the limelight, with many dominating the actives list. Leading the pack was investment holding firm, KLI Holdings, which saw about 20 million shares traded. The share ended up Singapore $0.19 at S$2.41. Idris
Hydraulic saw over 8.1 million shares traded.

Speculation and arbitraging were among the causes for the rally in Malaysian shares. Dealers said most were trading at a discount to their counter-parts on the Kuala Lumpur exchange. The re-rating of Malaysia's economy by some foreign funds also boosted sentiment, dealers said.
The UOB OTC index hit a high of 1,255.88 before settling at 1,251.05, up 10 points.
The foreign tranche of DBS led the gainers, rising S$0.40 to S$19.50 on 669,000 units while Singapore Press Holdings' foreign tranche fell S$1.30 to S$27.00 on 373,000 shares.
